_whyThisExists: `scripts/vulngate.py` fails the build on a reachable vulnerability. Some are not fixable by a
version bump, and a gate that cannot be made green teaches everyone to ignore the gate — the
exact failure `security.yml`'s header warns about. So the decision goes HERE, in a file a pull
request has to touch and a reviewer can read, instead of into a `|| true`.
An entry is not a dismissal. `vulngate.py` fails when an entry matches nothing (the
vulnerability is gone and the suppression is still live) and when one is past its `review_by`.
Both are deliberate build breaks. A suppression file without them only ever grows, and the
entry that silences the next real finding was added for a finding that no longer exists.

allow.why: Off-by-one in moby's PLUGIN PRIVILEGE VALIDATION — daemon code. kontra uses the docker CLIENT, and `docker/docker` ships daemon and client in one `+incompatible` module, so `cli.init` reaching `client.init` makes every daemon symbol init-reachable. The reported trace is package initialisation, not a call into plugin validation, and kontra never installs a docker plugin.
allow.fix_requires: github.com/moby/moby/v2 >= v2.0.0-beta.8. `github.com/docker/docker` has no fixed version and will not get one — the fix lives at a NEW module path, so this is an import rewrite across cli/deploy.go, cli/scale.go and cli/warden, onto a module still in beta.

allow.why: Same module, same shape, same reason: reported through `cli.init` → `client.init` → `api.init`, which is package initialisation of the API types the client needs. Not a call into the vulnerable path.
allow.fix_requires: github.com/moby/moby/v2 >= v2.0.0-beta.8, as above. The two advisories move together or not at all.
